📰|Sky News: The United States the nation that once imposed its will upon the entire planet is now being sidelined from the global stage. Not by its enemies, but by its own allies.

While Donald Trump tweets furiously on social media like a man shouting into the wilderness France, Japan, the Philippines, Britain, and dozens of other nations are quietly and systematically striking deals with Iran right behind his back.

What is unfolding now is not merely a bad week in the annals of Trump’s foreign policy; it is a comprehensive geopolitical realignment. The U.S.-led international order has come to an end, and the time has come to build something new.

France did not resort to military force; instead, it employed diplomacy. It went to the Security Council and exercised its veto power to prevent any military invasion or any forcible reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. It told Trump: "We will not fight to appease your ego, Donald; we will engage with Iran like adults."

Iran now controls the Strait of Hormuz, levying a toll ranging from one to three dollars on every barrel of oil that passes through. Rather than merely shouting in protest, France accepted this reality; it forged a partnership with Oman and engaged directly with Tehran.

Trump bankrupted casinos and corporations, and now he is bankrupting American foreign policy oblivious to the fact that the entire world is the one paying the price.

—————
📌 The United States has forfeited its role as the world’s sole leader, and its allies have begun to act with complete independence from American wishes.

📌 Trump remains detached from reality, contenting himself with "angry reactions" on social media while the actual geopolitical landscape shifts around him.  
📌 France emerges as a powerful alternative player, having employed smart diplomacy rather than military threats. France successfully circumvented U.S. intentions regarding the #Strait_of_Hormuz dossier, forging direct understandings with Iran to ensure the safe passage of its vessels. French President #Macron has called for the construction of a "third way"—an alternative path for nations that wish to avoid both subservience to China and exposure to the volatility of U.S. foreign policy.

📌 The New Reality in the Strait of Hormuz:
• International acknowledgment of Iran's *de facto* control over the world's most critical maritime corridor for oil shipments.
• Iran has become an indispensable diplomatic partner in ensuring global energy security a development that bolsters its international legitimacy despite U.S. sanctions.

📌 The Exclusion of the United States from New International Alliances:
• Nations such as Canada, Japan, India, Brazil, Australia, and the United Kingdom have begun constructing new trade and security networks that deliberately exclude the United States.
• A prevailing conviction among these nations is that "trust" in America has been irrevocably shattered and that rebuilding such trust would require decades, if indeed it remains possible at all.

📌 The Trump administration's conduct of foreign policy mirrors its failed management of its own business enterprises; it systematically dismantles alliances and agreements without offering any viable alternative plan, thereby driving U.S. global influence into "bankruptcy."

📌 The world no longer waits for America to put its own house in order; rather, it has already begun to organize itself independently of the United States. The French vessel that recently transited the Strait of Hormuz stands as tangible proof of this profound geopolitical shift.

Message to U.S. Citizens: Demonstration Alert: April 9 Protests at U.S. Embassy Manila
https://t.co/MqdISCsl0q

A protest is scheduled to take place at U.S. Embassy Manila on Thursday, April 9. Demonstrators are expected to assemble along Kalaw Avenue and begin marching toward the embassy at approximately 9:30 a.m.

The embassy has not received any credible threats of violence or observed any indications of potential unrest. Protests near the embassy have historically been peaceful. The U.S. embassy is scheduled to be closed April 9 for a local holiday, and no operational impacts are expected.

Actions to Take:
• U.S. citizens should avoid political demonstrations. Foreign nationals found engaging in a protest could be considered in violation of their immigration status.
• Exercise caution when in the vicinity of any large gatherings, as even peaceful rallies/demonstrations have the potential to turn violent without warning. Follow instructions from local authorities.
• Follow local media and government sources for updates on possible public demonstrations, including information on disruptions to traffic or public services.
• Enroll in the Smart Traveler Enrollment Program (https://t.co/q8w0nZfWZo) to receive Alerts and make it easier to locate you in an emergency.

———————————————————-

For further information and assistance:
• Enroll in the Smart Traveler Enrollment Program  (https://t.co/q8w0nZfWZo) to receive Alerts and make it easier to locate you in an emergency.
• Contact the U.S. Embassy in Manila, Philippines, located at 1201 Roxas Boulevard, at +(63) (2) 5301-2000, from 7:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Monday through Friday. After-hours emergency number for U.S. citizens is +(63) (2) 5301-2000.
• Call 1-888-407-4747 toll-free in the United States and Canada or 1-202-501-4444 from other countries from 8:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. Eastern Standard Time, Monday through Friday (except U.S. federal holidays).
• See the State Department’s travel website (https://t.co/Tiyt8sq7F9) for the Worldwide Caution, Travel Advisories, Alerts, and the Philippines Country Specific Information (https://t.co/ApMa3LxNZy).

Munster U20H Traffic Advisory

Supporters traveling to Sixmilebridge this evening for the Fulfil Munster GAA U20 Hurling game - Clare v Limerick are advised to access the venue via the old roads in light of the ongoing fuel protests on the motorways.

Limerick supporters should access Sixmilebridge via the Moylish & Cratloe back roads.

Clare supporters should access Sixmilebridge via the Quin & Newmarket on Fergus back roads.

Patrons are advised to travel early to avoid expected delays.
